claims.claim: Customer and government exposure is highly concentrated: one customer represented 82% of Q2 2026 revenue and 74% of first-half 2026 revenue, while government customers represented 92% of Q2 revenue and 89% of first-half revenue.
claims.use: Alpha risk-source support; concentration can amplify contract timing, procurement-policy and customer-specific execution sensitivity.

claims.claim: Liquidity is substantial but does not eliminate financing/dilution risk: at June 30, 2026 Infleqtion reported $59.3M cash and cash equivalents plus $522.5M available-for-sale securities, while also reporting a $54.4M first-half net loss and expecting continued operating losses; management states future equity or convertible financing could dilute stockholders if additional capital is raised.
claims.use: Alpha risk-source support; distinguish current liquidity runway from longer-term self-funding economics.

claims.claim: Revenue-recognition quality warrants explicit confidence treatment rather than a bearish conclusion: management identified immaterial errors related to revenue recognition and expected-loss methodology, while contract revenue relies materially on cost-to-cost progress estimates and timing of billings/cash collection.
claims.use: Alpha data-confidence/risk support; preserve as an evidence-quality sensitivity, not evidence of current fraud or business deterioration.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration creates sensitivity to a single customer's procurement, milestone timing and renewal behavior.
Government-heavy revenue mix exposes realized revenue to procurement policy, budget and contract timing even when technical execution is sound.
Longer-term funding needs could create dilution if commercialization does not mature before current liquidity is consumed.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong liquidity and improving commercialization coexist with concentrated revenue, continuing losses and accounting-estimate sensitivity.
contradictions.disposition: risk clarification for Alpha; not a present Beta blocker and not evidence that the commercialization thesis is false.

unknowns.unknown: Durability and renewal economics of the dominant customer relationship are not established by the cited filing.
The filing does not establish when quantum-computing commercialization becomes self-funding without additional capital.

falsifiers: Sustained diversification of revenue and receivables across independent commercial customers would materially reduce the concentration concern.
Repeatable positive operating cash flow excluding working-capital timing effects would weaken the financing/dilution concern.
Clean subsequent reporting without further revenue-recognition corrections, paired with cash/contract corroboration, would reduce the reporting-quality sensitivity.
